native.title: Authority is visible in the statement
native.caption: Four classes of statement. The four quadrants make statement authority and status explicit. (a) An observed source fact requires an opened source and a sentence-level citation. (b) A project decision records a choice with its rationale and version. (c) An open question preserves missing, conflicting or inaccessible evidence as unverified. (d) Future work is planned before implementation, review or measurement. Solid and dashed boundaries distinguish asserting and unresolved or intended classes. These classes are not an evidence ranking. The source-record illustration is AI-generated and conceptual.

caveats: The two representation topics for proteins and for complexes stay at worked deliberately. This repository holds no protein or complex artifact a reader can run, and building one would require protein data it does not ship, so those rows remain in the executable queue as work rather than as routing.

Two topics held at worked on 2026-09-10 were later closed by building rather than by rescoring, and both builds are additive to a synthetic sandbox that changes no empirical result. Computational limits and uncertainty gained an optimiser sweep reporting gradient evaluations, decision agreement and probability spread. Inductive-bias selection was in the same position on 2026-09-10 and was closed by building rather than by rescoring. The sandbox previously varied penalty strength inside one linear family, which is a different question, so a decision-stump arm was added to compare families under one selection rule.

A written lesson that supplies a worked case and an independent exercise with an answer is scored at worked, not at executable or assessed, unless a runnable artifact in this repository covers the same topic. Depth is ordinal here, so scoring a hand exercise as assessed would also claim an executable route that does not exist. This makes the executable and assessed lower bounds a floor rather than a reading of teaching quality.
Version 0.1 provides one substantive introduction per track but does not yet cover all 93 comparison topics at explained depth.

FreeSolv is a completed predictive baseline lab, and T15 is a completed retrospective teaching replay with assessed exercises. T05 has completed its paired frozen evaluation, but T15 had already exposed shared labels; no subsequent T05 retuning or independent-confirmation claim is supported. T11 has completed two within-system evaluations; their time-correlated frames are not pooled into biological replicates, and the locked artifact lacks per-frame Ridge predictions for an independent post-run Ridge recomputation.
No public deployment URL or public correction route was verified on 2026-09-04, so external content and code access remain unverified.
